about: L7 T5 golden set. Split into improvement and holdout before any run and before any tuning; questions and expected values are not edited after the first run, a change is a new version. Expected values are written from the synthetic fixtures (src/data/finance.ts, models, datasets), never copied from the code under test. Tuning may read improvement results only.
split: Stratified by domain. Improvement holds the copilot's own suggestions and their siblings; holdout holds paraphrases and questions not yet asked of the system.

metrics.tool_accuracy: Share of answers whose first tool call is the expected tool.
metrics.calculation_accuracy: Share of expected values found verbatim in the tool results.
metrics.unsupported_verified_claims: Count of answers whose result state is VERIFIED while the expected state is not VERIFIED or an expected value is missing, plus drafts shown to the analyst that the draft check would withhold. The pass rule needs 0 in the holdout.
metrics.citation_precision: Over finance answers: cited sources that give the claim's own value, over all cited sources.
metrics.latency_ms: Wall time of one ask, median.
metrics.cost_usd: Sum of each call's cost at the dated prices in src/lib/model.ts; 0 when no model is called.
metrics.n_and_se: n counts answers, q counts questions. Runs of a deterministic pipeline are not independent draws, so each standard error uses the q questions that contribute to its metric, sqrt(p(1-p)/q).

pass: The holdout shows 0 unsupported verified claims; the script exits non-zero otherwise. For the loop's deciding rule the holdout is run at least 3 times through the live model and its drafts are judged by a model other than the maker's.
judge: Drafts exist only when a live model writes them. Their judge is a model other than the maker's (Opus 5.5) and the product's (DeepSeek); proposed: Claude Sonnet through the Agent tool, n of at least 3, with the holdout's draft-level verdicts recorded beside the script's output.
